newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks seen eying record high at open.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks seen eying record high at open.

* Toronto stocks were expected on Thursday to take their direction from the U.S. jobs data due out before the bell. * Analysts said if data were as expected the market would climb to all-time high today.

Toronto stocks were expected to take their direction from the U.S. jobs data due out before the bell on Thursday, and analysts said the market would pass its life-time high if the numbers came in as expected.

"As long as the data comes in as expected or lower than expected, both the Dow and the TSE will push through the record highs, which they are just below now," MMS International technical analyst Katherine Beattie said.
She said if the data were stronger than expected the markets could drop more than 100 points in the session after powering ahead on Wednesday.
Beattie said a rebound in gold prices should help Toronto's gold sector regain some ground.

The Toronto Stock Exchange's 300 Composite Index climbed 111.30 points or about 1.7 percent to close on Wednesday at 6549.04, as investors celebrated a decision by the U.S. central bank to hold U.S. short-term interest rates steady.
The market is just a few ticks shy of its all-time high of 6557 set on June 16.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average surged 73 points to 7795 on Wednesday.

Market players had widely expected the U.S. Federal Reserve to keep rates unchanged after a two-day committee meeting, Beattie said, and focus would now shift to the August meeting of the Fed's policy arm.
The U.S. employment data due out at 0830 EDT/1230 GMT were considered the final hurdle for financial markets this week as U.S. markets take a holiday on Friday to celebrate Independence Day.

Analysts expected June non-farm payrolls to rise by about 222,000, after an increase of 138,000 in May. The unemployment rate was expected to hold steady at 4.8 percent, and average hourly earnings were seen rising by 0.4 percent.
--- STOCKS TO WATCH ---

* CanWest Global Communications Corp said on Wednesday a wholly owned subsidiary acquired 554,700 additional class B non-voting shares of WIC Western International Ltd at a price of C$24.50 a share. The purchase upped CanWest's stake in WIC to about 19.4 percent of the class B non-voting shares.
But CanWest repeated that it had no intention of making a takeover bid for its western rival. WIC defeated a hostile takeover bid by CanWest last year.
